authoredBy: main-lane Claude, 2026-08-13 — Year 1 after The Judges; the curriculum lane extends this to three years
principles: Announced, not chosen — the order is set for him; the pace is his
Mixed modality: narrative, doctrine, gospel, practice, epistle, history, hope — not book-by-book
Terms run 3 to 30 studies, never longer; units inside a term are 3-6 days
Hard texts are read whole, flagged ahead, never skipped
History is taught with the Bible open — every study anchors to a reading
Revisiting a book is a feature: deeper pass, new lens

terms.title: The Exile
terms.rationale: Judges ended with no king in Israel. The exile is what happened centuries later when the kings came and failed too — the covenant curses falling exactly as written, and God keeping covenant anyway, in a foreign land. From national amnesia to national catastrophe to a remnant walking home. This is the Old Testament's hinge, and most readers skip it.

units.label: The slow collapse — Manasseh to the fall
Jeremiah — the prophet who watched it happen
Daniel — faithful in Babylon
Coming home — Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai

terms.title: Justification
terms.rationale: Two terms of narrative failure — the judges' cycles, the exile's verdict — leave one question standing: how is anyone ever right with God? Six days on the hinge of the Reformation. Short on purpose: one doctrine, held up to the light until it catches.

units.label: The verdict — God counts the ungodly righteous
The exchange — Christ our righteousness

terms.title: The Gospel of Mark
terms.rationale: After the doctrine of justification, watch the Justifier walk. Mark is Peter's memories at a sprint — 'immediately' more than forty times — the shortest gospel and the least polished, which is exactly its authority. The kingdom arrives, is misunderstood, and goes to a cross on purpose.

units.label: The kingdom arrives in a hurry
Who then is this? — power and misunderstanding
The road down — discipleship toward Jerusalem
The Passion according to Peter

terms.title: Giving a Reason
terms.rationale: Study that never leaves the room goes stale. Five days on witness — not technique, and not a personality transplant: hope, given with gentleness and respect, by people who were asked. Watch Jesus with one woman, Paul with the philosophers and with a king, and then find your own two minutes.

units.label: Always ready — hope with gentleness

terms.title: Romans
terms.rationale: The year's deep one, at the cap on purpose: thirty studies, no more. Paul's gospel laid out whole — indictment, gift, union, the Spirit, Israel, and a life poured out in response. You have read Romans before; this pass is slower, with the confessions at hand and your own open questions waiting in the margins.
terms.hardNote: Unit four sits in Romans 9–11 — election, hardening, and the mercy of God. It will be read whole, in order, without flinching and without softening. The confessions are at hand and the tone is Paul's own: not a puzzle to win, a doxology to reach.
terms.secondNote: You have walked Romans devotionally before. This is the 300-level pass — slower, unit by unit, with the doctrine load-bearing.

units.label: No one righteous — the indictment
Reckoned — Abraham's children by faith
United — dead to sin, alive in the Spirit
The mystery — Israel and the mercy of God
Living sacrifices — the gospel embodied

terms.title: The First Five Centuries
terms.rationale: The faith did not skip from Acts to your church. Martyrs held it, councils defined it, Augustine defended it — the vocabulary of orthodoxy was forged in fire and argument. History taught with the Bible open: every day anchors to the texts the church was dying for and defining.

units.label: Blood and testimony — the martyr church
Nicaea — the Son, very God of very God
Augustine — grace against the current

terms.title: Hope — the Last Things
terms.rationale: End the year facing forward. Death, resurrection, return, renewal — hope as doctrine, not as mood. Six days standing where Paul stood: if Christ is not raised, nothing here was worth a single morning; since he is, everything was.

units.label: What we await
